clause_that_reaches_it: THE WORK — the prose, the screenplay, the thing being created — is protected AT ALL COSTS and is version-controlled: every change to it is retained.

Deleting an annotation is an act on the annotation layer; letting it silently un-apply a manuscript change the writer had already accepted would let an annotation-layer gesture rewrite the work without going through the work's own version-controlled path. Leaving the applied text alone keeps the two layers separate, which is what the tier requires. Cited as a root because no sub-ruling partitions the annotation layer against the manuscript in this direction — RULING-25 does so only for time travel.

why_in_scope: R22's scope is an expectation Maugham created being contradicted by the outcome, and its settled list already contains a rewind case ('stale cursor silent no-op') on the same control. The rewind scrubber names a moment and promises the document as it was then; over an unsorted mirror it renders a state the document never held — the peer's later text shown at the writer's own earlier moment — with no signal. `Deriver.derive(ops:upTo:)`'s refusal to re-sort is correct and documented (a timeline prefix must respect its caller's order); the broken party is the premise it is handed, stated in `currentFoldBasis`'s own comment as an invariant that does not hold. Filing this on the annotations module rather than on rewind because the appends that break the ordering are this module's, and because it is the thread the Rewind verifier left unchased. Reachability needs a second Mac whose clock is ahead; PRINCIPLE-4 governs the priority, and AREA.md's existing acceptance of a clock-skew inversion is about which BOOTSTRAP wins, not about this premise.

clause_that_reaches_it: A suggestion whose quoted phrase can no longer be found in the writer's paragraph MUST NOT be applied. It is refused, the writer is told why, and they may ask again. Maugham never guesses where an AI-authored change belongs.
why_in_scope: This is RULING-5's own case, verbatim, still live at the accept path. The quoted phrase is gone; the suggestion is applied anyway; and the guess Maugham makes about where it belongs is the largest one available — the whole paragraph. `SuggestionSplice.apply` documents the fallback as 'the safe fallback for a lost anchor', which is the reading R5 was written to overturn: the ruling's stated consequence accepts that 'a suggestion the writer still wants becomes unusable after any nearby edit', deliberately, 'as the price of never mis-placing AI text'. Measured: 'She was livid about the whole business.' with a lost 'very angry → furious' anchor accepts to 'furious'. The pane's preview reads 'very angry → furious' throughout, because `SuggestionDisplay.before` returns `span.quote` for an unresolvable span, so the surface promises a two-word swap and the outcome is a sentence replaced by one word.
call_path: MCP add_suggested_change with a quote → AnnotationsPane row → the writer rewrites the sentence → Accept (via the stale confirm's 'Apply anyway', or with no confirm at all inside the burst window, M5-AN-050) → Document.acceptAnnotation → SuggestionSplice.apply → SpanAnchorResolver returns nil → `return bare`

clause_that_reaches_it: It is refused, the writer is told why, and they may ask again.
why_in_scope: The second face of M5-AN-049, filed separately because it is a different mechanism with a different fix. R5 requires the writer to be TOLD; the nearest thing Maugham has is the pane's 'Paragraph has changed since this suggestion' confirm, and that confirm is gated on `annotation.isStale`, which is read off a cache no text-edit path invalidates. With the cache warm — which a rendered pane guarantees — the writer rewrites the paragraph and the row still reports itself fresh, so no confirm appears and the paragraph is replaced with no warning of any kind. The protection is not merely weaker than R5 requires; inside the burst window it is absent.

reason: Cross-device merge bookkeeping. The sticky flag is an optimisation; that a peer's annotation appears is the op log's merge contract, ruled nowhere.

Merge correctness — 'two devices with identical logs must derive identical text' is an architectural invariant (AREA.md), not a product decision. Recorded because it is what confines M5-AN-047's damage to rewind.

RULING-13's scope is a paragraph whose IDENTITY is not recovered, where annotations move with the text and are marked stale. A deleted paragraph is not that — there is no text to move with. The deriver does mark these stale, which is R13's shape applied by coincidence rather than by reach. Raised as GAP-A5, and note it is what makes M5-AN-030's dead Revert reachable.
